title: Length-consistency test on encoded inputs
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $C_w,c_w$ be natural numbers, and let $x,U$ be finite binary strings. For natural numbers $t,a,j$ satisfying $j\le |x|+1$ and $j<2^{C_w(|x|+1)^{c_w}}$, the length-consistency atom evaluates to true on the encoded tuple formed from $x,U$, the width-$C_w(|x|+1)^{c_w}$ binary words for $t$ and $a$, the string of $j$ ones, and a string of $C_w(|x|+1)^{c_w}-\ell$ zeros, where $\ell$ is the binary length of $j$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet
caveat: The claim's encoded input and length-consistency atom depend on several upstream constructions whose informal definitions were not supplied, so the wording describes their roles without spelling out their full encodings.
